challenge.exploration_summary: The project is a small ANSI C library with core parser, printer, tree manipulation, and comparison APIs in cJSON.c/cJSON.h, plus optional JSON pointer/patch utilities in cJSON_Utils.*. I chose the core cJSON module because object lookup and comparison are well-covered, central to the public API, and had a clear limitation around key/value strings containing decoded null bytes.
challenge.feature_spec: Add length-aware object member lookup APIs: cJSON_GetObjectItemWithLength, cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitiveWithLength, and cJSON_HasObjectItemWithLength. The core parser now tracks decoded object key lengths and string/raw value lengths, allowing exact lookup of keys containing embedded null bytes or keys supplied as non-null-terminated slices. cJSON_Compare also uses the tracked lengths so embedded-null strings and object keys compare correctly.
challenge.feature_rationale: cJSON already parses JSON escape sequences such as \u0000 into in-memory strings, but the existing object lookup and comparison paths relied on NUL-terminated string functions. Length-aware lookup belongs in cJSON.c because it extends the same object traversal semantics as cJSON_GetObjectItem while preserving existing APIs for callers with ordinary C strings.
challenge.bug_description: The case-insensitive length comparator returns equality as soon as it reaches an embedded NUL byte, even when the requested comparison length continues past that byte. This causes length-aware case-insensitive object lookup and cJSON_Compare to treat distinct decoded keys such as "A\u0000B" and "A\u0000C" as the same key, returning the wrong member or reporting unequal objects as equal.

findings.description: The submitted case-insensitive length comparison stopped as soon as it saw a NUL byte, so equal-length keys such as {'a','\0','b'} and {'a','\0','c'} compared equal. This made cJSON_GetObjectItemWithLength and case-insensitive object comparison return the wrong member for embedded-NUL keys.

The submitted duplicate path copied tracked string/key lengths but still used the strlen-based cJSON_strdup helper for valuestring and object keys. Duplicating a parsed item containing an embedded NUL allocated only the prefix while preserving the longer length, so later cJSON_Compare or length-aware lookup could read past the duplicated allocation.

The applied PR did not keep the public cJSON struct and API declarations in the header synchronized with cJSON.c; the implementation referenced string_length, valuestring_length, and the new lookup symbols while the header did not declare them. This broke compilation for users including cJSON.h.

self_review.fix_explanation: Repaired the malformed applied changes, added the length fields and new lookup declarations to cJSON.h, made the case-insensitive length comparison inspect every byte in the supplied length, updated successful string/key mutation paths to maintain the tracked lengths, and added an exact-length duplicate helper so embedded-NUL strings and object keys are copied with their full tracked size.
